chapter: Instruments, first jobs and the regional scene
title: Learning the shoemaking trade
summary: Joe could repair any shoe and his father kept insisting he learn the trade as a fallback.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let me get a little back to the shoemaking business. I know it doesn't have too much to do with music, but I just wanted to ask you this. You learned the shoemaking trade pretty good, then.
Oh, I got so that I could practically make a pair of shoes.
If I came to you with a pair of shoes and said, "Look at this sole," could you do that?

Oh, I could repair any shoe that was made. Now, making a pair of shoes... In the first place, to make a good pair of shoes, you've got to make a lasp(?), which is (?) the shape of the foot. And my Dad had just acres of lasp(?) shoes. Well, sure. In fact, I've got some shoemaker tools now that I can put rubber heels on, or if I have to have rubber caps, I can do it.

I know it's kind of hard for you to remember, but how old were you when you finally told your Dad that you weren't going to fool around with the shoemaking business and wanted to make music your career? Do you remember?
Oh, I told him that many a time, heh-heh, but he didn't ...(?)... with the shoes.
It didn't sink in too well.

He kind of had a problem(?)... But he used to say, "Look, I know you want to travel with the circus, Joe, and when you get old enough you'll be able to go." But he says, "You remember, people are always going to be

wearing shoes, see, and if something happens you will always be able to make a living. So you learn this trade."
Anyway, me and my brother kind of kept this band together until it was a pretty good band. We got various little jobs when we were 16 or 17 years old...
